problemStatement.formal: Formalize ordinal partition relations such as omega_3 -> (omega_2, omega)^2 and related GCH/CH questions, with weak consequences from Erdos-Dushnik-Miller and independence-style assumptions from Todorcevic and PFA.
problemStatement.plain: Backfill the metadata for the Erdos 1172 ordinal partition scaffold: definitions of unbalanced and balanced partition relations, the four CH/GCH questions, provable weak forms, and the set-theoretic axioms used for independence context.
whyMatters: Ordinal partition relations are a core meeting point of infinitary combinatorics and set-theoretic hypotheses.
The Lean file gives reusable definitions and weak consequences even though the original Erdos questions remain open.
The metadata should distinguish proved ordinal arithmetic from axiomatized deep set-theory inputs.

proven: `OrdPartitionRel`, `BalancedPartitionRel`, `GCH`, `CH`, and `gch_implies_ch` set up the formal language for the four questions.
`omega1_lt_omega2`, `omega2_lt_omega3`, `omega_lt_omega1`, and related positivity lemmas supply the ordinal arithmetic base.
`partition_independence`, `q3_first_target_large`, and `q2_targets_lt_omega3` record independence context and target-size checks.
open: `erdos_dushnik_miller`, `todorcevic_negative`, and `pfa_positive` are axioms in `Erdos1172Problem.lean`; the file has zero sorries.
The four headline questions `question1` through `question4` are definitions rather than solved theorems.
knownResults.goal: Make the ordinal-partition scaffold discoverable while marking the deep set-theoretic hypotheses as axioms.
